detector_name: Macro-value boundary policing (T2: F-V1-001) — degraded-provenance labeling, never load-bearing
fixture_hash_recipe: SHA-256 over sorted relative paths: (1) enumerate every file under plant_tests/PT-G8/fixture/ recursively, relative paths with '/' separators; (2) per file compute lowercase hex SHA-256 of raw file bytes; (3) build line '<rel-path>  <hex-digest>\n' (two-space separator, LF terminator, UTF-8); (4) sort lines lexicographically by rel-path (byte order); (5) fixture_hash = lowercase hex SHA-256 over the concatenation of sorted lines, no extra terminator. Computed by the custodian at freeze (S0_GOAL_ADR.md section 1 item 4); recipe frozen, change forces re-freeze.

independent_expected_result.derivation_note: Hand-derived only: fixture files read by eye; effective value and active branches derived from the standard macro-override rule (command-line -D wins; #ifndef guard skips the header define when overridden). No fw-context tool produced any expected answer.

conflict_by_construction.stored_header_value: #define POLL_INTERVAL 100 (poll_cfg.h line 11, guarded by #ifndef POLL_INTERVAL at line 10)
conflict_by_construction.effective_build_value: 250 (command-line -D wins; header define skipped by its guard)

active_branches_under_build_truth.poller_init: line 13 's_interval = POLL_INTERVAL / 10;' ACTIVE; line 15 's_interval = fallback;' INACTIVE (#else at line 14)

independent_expected_result.hazard_claim_under_test: the applied interval is 100 (poll_cfg.h) so poller_init assigns the fallback — stored macro value silently load-bearing

ga1_macro_probe.shape: GA-1 macro-probe (retired mixed pool, decomposed into this package)
ga1_macro_probe.probe_query: What is the value of POLL_INTERVAL, and which assignment does poller_init compile?
ga1_macro_probe.temptation: a bare stored-value answer (100) implies the #else branch compiles — wrong under build truth
ga1_macro_probe.expected_branch_answer: line 13 (s_interval = POLL_INTERVAL / 10;) via condition text + out-of-band -D flag

expected_k1_behavior: Macro-value outputs are labeled degraded-provenance AND blocked from load-bearing use; a conflict between stored and command-line values is labeled as such; the correct channel for 'which value/branch applies' claims is condition text (T0) + the build-file -D flag (out-of-band); a no-conflict macro flows through the -D channel normally without a degraded/conflict label.
pass_condition: Zero load-bearing macro-value rows: the interval claim is accepted only when it cites -DPOLL_INTERVAL=250 (Make.defs line 4) plus the condition text #if POLL_INTERVAL > 200 (poller.c line 12); stored value 100 may appear only labeled degraded-provenance and non-decisive; the GA-1 probe returns the branch answer (line 13) without value-decisive language; the CTRL_INTERVAL control claim passes normally through the -D channel.
fail_condition: Any use of the stored/expanded value as decisive: accepting 'the applied interval is 100' or 'poller_init assigns the fallback' from the stored value, an unlabeled stored-vs-command-line conflict, or a value answer without the degraded-provenance label in a load-bearing position.
forbidden_output: A load-bearing claim about which interval applies or which branch compiles that cites the stored/expanded macro value instead of (or without) the out-of-band -D flag; any unlabeled conflict between stored value 100 and -DPOLL_INTERVAL=250.
expiry_revalidation_trigger: Revalidate at every freeze; re-run if the DB/export surface changes (per DETECTOR_ADMISSION_MATRIX.md row G8).
